points.reason: This generate block only ties reg_file(0) to a constant at line 117 and provides no attacker-controlled observation, modification, or blocking mechanism.
rd_i can overwrite a selected register when the write condition passes, while reset clears entries and rf_wb_en can withhold a required write-back at lines 106-110.
The process writes rd_i into reg_file under rf_we and exposes selected entries on rs1_o and rs2_o, while rf_we can suppress a required update.
opa_addr selects the register returned on rs1_o, while rf_we and its control inputs select or suppress the register write.
The process returns indexed reg_file values on rs1_o and rs2_o, and reset or failure to receive the clocked update can leave those operand outputs unavailable.
The process returns the indexed reg_file value on rs3_o, and the clocked update can be stalled so the required operand is not delivered.
ctrl_i.ir_funct12 is copied into rs3_addr and selects which register value rs3_read exposes on rs3_o.
